analysis.session_summary: The day was dominated by the 14:30 US/Canada employment releases. Non-Farm Employment Change +2 more beat at 162K vs 55K, lifting USD by 0.334% and USD/CAD by 65.7 pips, while Canada's Employment Change missed at -41.7K vs 15.1K and made CAD the weakest major at -0.334%. AUD and NZD outperformed while CHF and JPY lagged, leaving DXY up 22.7 points and SPX down 22.5 points. Several intraday legs lacked clear catalysts, and Ivey PMI and BOE Governor Bailey produced only muted reactions, pointing to flow-driven chop into the close.

themes.theme: Strong US data anchors the USD bid
themes.evidence: Non-Farm Employment Change +2 more beat at 162K vs 55K with USD impulse +0.334%; DXY +22.7 points and USD/JPY +67.3 pips, USD/CHF +34.2 pips followed.
AUD +0.306% and NZD +0.233% versus majors; AUD/USD +4.8 pips, NZD/USD +0.1 pips, AUD/CHF +28.4 pips and NZD/CHF +20.2 pips.

themes.theme: CAD weakest on large jobs miss
themes.evidence: Employment Change printed -41.7K vs 15.1K forecast; own-currency impulse -0.252%; CAD strength -0.334% and USD/CAD +65.7 pips.

themes.theme: Most intraday swings lacked clean macro catalysts
themes.evidence: Many legs in EUR/USD, USD/JPY, GBP/USD carry confidence none; only the US/Canada employment releases and Ivey PMI produced measurable reactions.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped in two main legs—a -37.3-pip decline with no clear catalyst and a +20.8-pip rebound—leaving it mid-range with no single driver.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD saw multiple two-sided legs; UK construction output contributed -10.1 pips to one down leg, but a larger -38.0-pip drop had no news, leaving flow in control.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD ground higher in small choppy legs, with only Ivey PMI adding a partial +2.9-pip push, ending firm.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD round-tripped, with an early +29.3-pip up leg offset by later dips, finishing nearly flat.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY whipsawed through a 143.6-pip day with alternating legs and no single catalyst until Ivey PMI added +23.6 pips to the last up leg.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF climbed in a long +54.1-pip leg then retraced -24.0 pips, reflecting broad USD strength.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD spiked on the dual employment surprise and then gave back -29.8 pips, ending firm but off the high.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF built gains in a +36.9-pip main leg and held most of it, ending higher.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY was a violent round trip with a -160.1-pip down leg partly driven by US employment data and a +83.9-pip late bounce on Ivey PMI.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD chopped through alternating legs, with a +32.7-pip up move and a +19.2-pip reaction to US data, ending slightly higher.
leg_notes.EUR/GBP: EUR/GBP stayed inside a tight 16.0-pip daily range, with only minor reactions to Bailey and Canadian data, ending nearly unchanged.
leg_notes.AUD/CHF: AUD/CHF recovered from an early dip and rallied +30.3 pips, helped by US employment data and broad CHF weakness.
leg_notes.NZD/CHF: NZD/CHF built on a +28.5-pip up leg and ended higher despite a late drag.
leg_notes.USD/SEK: USD/SEK spiked higher, corrected sharply after the employment release, then re-accelerated to a large net gain.
leg_notes.USD/NOK: USD/NOK chopped violently, with the NFP beat causing a +375.9-pip surge that largely stuck, leaving a moderate net gain.
leg_notes.USD/ZAR: USD/ZAR swung between large up and down legs; despite a +775.7-pip NFP-driven move, it ended lower on the day.
leg_notes.USD/MXN: USD/MXN sold off in a -864.0-pip leg with only a partial -131.8-pip Ivey PMI contribution, ending near the lows.
leg_notes.Brent/USD: Brent round-tripped through a -262.2-pip decline and +250.5-pip bounce to close nearly flat.

polarity_reads.read: A normal 0.334% USD impulse on a 162K vs 55K beat shows USD remains bid on strong data; no inversion means the market had not already front-run the beat.
A normal -0.252% CAD impulse after a -41.7K print confirms CAD downside; with CAD already the weakest major at -0.334%, positioning remains short CAD.
A 64.3 vs 56.2 beat produced a muted -0.021% basket move, signalling CAD upside was limited or offset by broader USD/JPY and CHF flows.
A muted -0.008% basket move implies sterling was insensitive to Bailey, leaving GBP driven by flow rather than policy comments.

scenarios.name: USD consolidates after payrolls
scenarios.thesis: The 14:30 US employment beat has been absorbed; DXY holds its 22.7-point gain while EUR/USD and USD/JPY settle into their measured ranges.
triggers: No high-impact calendar ahead; measured ranges in EUR/USD and USD/JPY contain price
scenarios.invalidation: EUR/USD breaking 1.16199 or USD/JPY breaking 156.031 would shift the tape away from consolidation.

USD/JPY finished at 0.51 of its 143.6-pip range after whipsawing.
USD/CAD closed at 0.65 of its 101.0-pip range after the jobs spike.

scenarios.thesis: AUD and NZD lead the strength map, and their crosses against CHF and USD continue to build on measured gains.
triggers: AUD/USD holds above 0.72098 close, NZD/USD above 0.58887 close
scenarios.invalidation: AUD/USD losing 0.72098 and NZD/USD losing 0.58887 would negate the upside.

scenarios.thesis: After the NFP surge, USD pairs unwind some of the move; EUR/USD and GBP/USD extend their late rebounds while USD/CHF and USD/CAD pull back.
scenarios.invalidation: USD/CHF breaking 0.80926 and USD/CAD breaking 1.38367 would signal renewed USD buying instead.

GBP/USD late up leg was +21.4 pips.

risks.why_it_matters: DXY +22.7 and USD +0.227% vs majors; further strength would pressure EUR/USD and GBP/USD.
AUD/NZD are already outperforming; if risk sentiment turns after SPX -22.5, the high-beta longs look stretched.
Several legs had no clear catalyst and Iran/Trump items appeared nearby; headline-driven gaps can be sharp in USD/ZAR, USD/MXN, Brent.
